title: Exchange of the trace maps: evaluation and support
statement:
Let $(f,g):(C,c)\to(D,b)$ be a proper pushforward diagram of
[def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] (no Cartesian leg square, no properness
over $s$), with the notation and admissibility of
[def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Then:

1. *(evaluation)* as maps $Rq_*P_X\to R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$,
$$
\delta_{K'}\circ\rho_f=R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\circ Rq_*\delta_K ;
$$
1. *(support)* as maps
$Rg_*Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}=Ri_{b*}Rh_*\omega_{F_c}\to Rb^!R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y$,
$$
Rb^!\bigl(R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\bigr)\circ\mathsf E\circ Rg_*\zeta_c
=\zeta_b\circ Ri_{b*}\tau_h ,
$$
where the source identification is $gi_c=i_bh$.

Moreover, for a Cartesian square $(\beta',\alpha',\beta,\alpha)$
($\beta:V\to W$, $\alpha:U\to W$ proper, $V'=V\times_WU$) the exceptional
adjoint of the right-adjoint base-change isomorphism
$R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\cong R\beta^!R\alpha_*$ (the mate of
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$) is
$R\beta_!R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\cong R\alpha_!R\beta'_!R\beta'^!
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}R\alpha_*$, the composition law followed by the
counit of $\beta'$.

proof.text:
Work at the finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$ inherited from [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward], with the constructible exceptional adjoints of [def-trf-admissibility]. The concrete operation package [prop-functor-package] supplies the proper identifications, compact-support composition, projection and exchange maps on these domains. In particular no ambient exceptional adjoint, and no properness of a structure morphism, is used. We use the adjunction-compatible exceptional composition comparison: the right adjoint of $Rv_!Ru_!$ is $Ru^!Rv^!$, since its Hom bijection is the composite of the two adjunction bijections. Conjugating the compact-support composition isomorphism as in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] gives $R(vu)^!\cong Ru^!Rv^!$. Applied to the identity of $Ru^!Rv^!N$, the two inverse Hom bijections give the counit
$$\varepsilon_{vu,N}=\varepsilon_{v,N}\circ Rv_!(\varepsilon_{u,Rv^!N}).$$
This also checks its normalization: the two units and counits in the conjugation formula cancel by the triangle identities. Associativity of the left composition comparisons [thm-sf-comp-composition] implies associativity of their conjugates, because conjugation reverses composition. These are assertions about the specified constructible adjunctions, so the stronger ambient hypothesis in some older mate lemmas is unnecessary.

source.place: Preliminaries for the last assertion and support: pasted exceptional counits

proof.text:
For the last assertion put $T=\operatorname{Ex}_!:L\alpha^*R\beta_!\to R\beta'_!L\alpha'^*$ and let $\Theta:R\beta_!R\alpha'_*\cong R\alpha_*R\beta'_!$ be compact-support composition along $\beta\alpha'=\alpha\beta'$. The base change $\alpha'$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The normalization lemma [lem-trf-compact-support-exchange-counit] gives
$$\varepsilon_\alpha\circ L\alpha^*\Theta=R\beta'_!\varepsilon_{\alpha'}\circ T R\alpha'_* .\tag{*}$$
Let $B:R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!\to R\beta^!R\alpha_*$ be the conjugate of $T$. Substituting into [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], its exceptional adjoint has ordinary $L\alpha^*\dashv R\alpha_*$ transpose
$$\varepsilon_{\beta'}\circ R\beta'_!\varepsilon_{\alpha'}\circ T R\alpha'_*R\beta'^!.$$
The proposed adjoint $R\alpha_*\varepsilon_{\beta'}\circ\Theta R\beta'^!$ has the same transpose: apply (*) at $R\beta'^!N$, then use naturality of $\varepsilon_\alpha$ for $\varepsilon_{\beta',N}$. Injectivity of the two Hom bijections proves the last assertion. Invertibility of $B$ follows because $T$ is an isomorphism by the compact-support base change of [prop-functor-package](4) and conjugation preserves isomorphisms. The ordinary adjunction used here is [fix-prop-adjunctions](1); the exceptional adjunctions are those fixed in step 1.

source.place: The last assertion: explicit double transpose and counit normalization

proof.text:
Put $L=D_XK$, and consider $B=Y\times_sY$, $U=X\times_sY$, $V=Y\times_sX$, $T=X\times_sX$, with $a=f\times1:U\to B$, $b=1\times f:V\to B$, $r=1\times f:T\to U$, $t=f\times1:T\to V$. Thus $ar=bt=q$, and these four arrows are proper base changes of $f$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Put $M=\operatorname{pr}_X^*K$ on $U$, $N=\operatorname{pr}_X^*L$ on $V$. By [def-sf-kv-maps](i), $\Pi_f$ is the inverse relative product for $a,b;M,N$, preceded by the two proper exchanges identifying $Rf_*K\boxtimes Rf_*L$ with $Ra_*M\otimes Rb_*N$. Apply [lem-trf-relative-kunneth-counit] to this relative product: its transpose is $r^*\varepsilon_{a,M}\otimes t^*\varepsilon_{b,N}$. The two preceding exchanges have transposes $\operatorname{pr}_X^*\varepsilon_f$ by the unit--square--counit formula of [def-exchange-projection]. Substitution and naturality of the counits therefore give
$$\varepsilon_q\circ q^*\Pi_f=\varepsilon_f\boxtimes\varepsilon_f.\tag{**}$$
The identifications $r^*M\otimes t^*N=K\boxtimes L$ are the product and monoidal pullback comparisons in [def-sf-kv-maps]. All inputs, including $L=D_XK$, have bounded constructible finite-Tor amplitude by [prop-functor-package](7). This derives the characterization of the specified inverse external Künneth map from the general relative product lemma, rather than assuming that any Künneth isomorphism has this transpose.

source.place: Evaluation, the claim: transpose of the specified inverse Künneth map

proof.text:
The diagonal square $q\Delta_X=\Delta_Yf$ is merely commutative. Define its ordinary exchange $\mathrm{Ex}:\Delta_Y^*Rq_*\to Rf_*\Delta_X^*$ by the general mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: its $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ transpose is
$$f^*\Delta_Y^*Rq_*=\Delta_X^*q^*Rq_*\xrightarrow{\Delta_X^*\varepsilon_q}\Delta_X^*.$$
In particular we do not apply a Cartesian base-change theorem to this square. By (**) in step 3 the transpose of $\mathrm{Ex}\circ\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$ is $\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$. This is exactly the transpose defining $\mu_f$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], so
$$\mathrm{Ex}\circ\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f=\mu_f.$$
Also $\mu_f$ respects tensor symmetry: after transposition its two candidate composites are respectively $\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$ followed by the symmetry and the symmetry followed by $\varepsilon_f\otimes\varepsilon_f$, which agree by naturality of the symmetry. This comparison uses the ordinary adjunction of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1).

source.place: Evaluation, diagonal exchange and the multiplication claim

proof.text:
Take $\Delta_Y^*\dashv R\Delta_{Y*}$ adjoints, using [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). By the definitions of evaluation kernels and $\rho_f$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps], the adjoint of the left side of (1) is
$$\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_{K'}(1\otimes\chi_f)\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f^{-1},\qquad
\overline{\mathrm{ev}}=\mathrm{ev}\circ\mathrm{sym}.$$
Naturality of the ordinary counit identifies the adjoint of the right side with $\tau_f\,Rf_*\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_K\,\mathrm{Ex}$. Precompose both arrows with the isomorphism $\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$. Step 4 changes the second arrow into $\tau_f Rf_*\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_K\mu_f$. The tensor--Hom transpose defining $\chi_f$, and the symmetry compatibility of $\mu_f$ just checked, give
$$\tau_f Rf_*\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_K\mu_f
=\overline{\mathrm{ev}}_{K'}(1\otimes\chi_f).$$
Cancel $\Delta_Y^*\Pi_f$ and use injectivity of the diagonal adjunction bijection. This proves (1).

source.place: Evaluation (1), final diagonal and tensor--Hom adjunctions

proof.text: For support, the two fixed squares are Cartesian by [prop-trf-fixed-square-cartesian]. Since $X$ and $Y$ are separated, their diagonals are closed immersions by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Their base changes $i_c,i_b$ are closed immersions by [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image]. Thus $\Delta_X,\Delta_Y,i_c,i_b$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and their compact-support direct images agree with their ordinary direct images by [prop-functor-package](3). The maps $g$ and $f$ are proper by the pushforward hypothesis, and $h,q$ are proper by [lem-trf-fixed-map-proper]. There is no properness assertion about $c,b,d_c,d_b$ or the structure maps.

source.place: Support (2), geometry of the two fixed squares

proof.text:
Apply step 2 to the fixed square, with $(\alpha,\alpha',\beta,\beta')=(\Delta_X,i_c,c,d_c)$. The inverse right-adjoint fixed-square base change is the map used to define $\zeta_c$ by [thm-trf-fixed-point-base-change] and [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. The canonical functorial dualizing identification of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition] gives $Rd_c^!\omega_X\cong\omega_{F_c}$. Thus the exceptional adjoint of $\zeta_c$ is
$$Rc_!Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}
 \cong Rc_!Ri_{c!}Rd_c^!\omega_X
 \cong R\Delta_{X!}Rd_{c!}Rd_c^!\omega_X
 \xrightarrow{R\Delta_{X!}\varepsilon_{d_c}}R\Delta_{X*}\omega_X.$$
For $b$, the parameters in step 2 are $(\Delta_Y,i_b,b,d_b)$, with proper $\Delta_Y,i_b$ by step 6. The definition of $\zeta_b$ and the dualizing comparison $Rd_b^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_{F_b}$ therefore give its exceptional adjoint as
$$Rb_!Ri_{b*}\omega_{F_b}
 \cong Rb_!Ri_{b!}Rd_b^!\omega_Y
 \cong R\Delta_{Y!}Rd_{b!}Rd_b^!\omega_Y
 \xrightarrow{R\Delta_{Y!}\varepsilon_{d_b}}R\Delta_{Y*}\omega_Y.$$
The two displayed maps retain $Rd_{c!}$ and $Rd_{b!}$; neither fixed-locus projection was assumed proper.

source.place: Support (2), exceptional adjoints of the support isomorphisms

proof.text:
Take the $Rb_!\dashv Rb^!$ adjoints of both sides of (2). The adjunction is the specified one of [def-trf-admissibility]. For the left side, the defining transpose of $\mathsf E$ in [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps] says
$$\varepsilon_b\,Rb_!\mathsf E=Rq_*\varepsilon_c\,\Xi.$$
Counit naturality therefore gives
$$R\Delta_{Y*}\tau_f\;Rq_*\bigl(\varepsilon_c\,Rc_!\zeta_c\bigr)\;\Xi.$$
Insert step 7. The source identifies, using properness of $g,i_c,q,\Delta_X,f$ and the composition law, with
$$Rb_!Rg_*Ri_{c*}\omega_{F_c}
 \cong Rq_*R\Delta_{X*}Rd_{c!}\omega_{F_c}
 \cong R\Delta_{Y*}Rf_*Rd_{c!}\omega_{F_c}.$$
The arrow under this identification is
$$R\Delta_{Y*}\bigl(\tau_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{d_c}\bigr).$$
By the pasted-counit calculation in step 1 and the functorial dualizing identifications of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition], the inner map is the counit of $R(fd_c)_!\dashv R(fd_c)^!$ at $\omega_Y$, with source $R(fd_c)_!\omega_{F_c}$.

For the right side of (2), first insert $Ri_{b*}\tau_h$ and then take the exceptional adjoint of $\zeta_b$ found in step 7. Its value is
$$R\Delta_{Y*}\bigl(\varepsilon_{d_b}\circ Rd_{b!}\tau_h\bigr),$$
with source identified as $R\Delta_{Y*}Rd_{b!}Rh_*\omega_{F_c}$. Here $\tau_h$ is precisely the exceptional counit after the dualizing identification by [def-trf-kernel-pushforward-maps]. Thus step 1 identifies the inner composite with the counit for $d_bh$ at $\omega_Y$. The defining equalities $i_bh=gi_c$ and $d_bh=fd_c$ of [def-trf-coefficient-pushforward] identify this source with that in step 8 and this counit with the one in step 8. The two identifications agree by the associative composition law of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and its adjoint normalization from step 1; the dualizing comparisons agree by functoriality in [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]. Therefore the exceptional adjoints, and hence the original maps, agree. This proves (2), using only the two fixed squares as Cartesian squares.

source.place: Support (2), right exceptional adjoint and equality
